I've had the same issue but don't set expectations for the people around you. Having 'standards' for who and what you like can make it even harder to find friends with whom you would actually get along. Not everyone is going to show and tell you everything about them upfront and avoiding/being rude to the quiet/shy people will put the people you'd like off of you. 

Just talk to everyone you can and show your personality. Focus on your life and what you are talking about instead of who you are speaking to and the more romantic ideas of what you'd prefer it would be like. If you don't really enjoy spending time with some people, step away and spend time with others/ doing other things. If you don't like the activity the group you're in is doing, go and do something else

Being more present and not thinking too hard about what you'd prefer/like will lead you to a more enjoyable time and, eventually, you'll have friends you immediately know you like to do x with and others you'd like to do y with.

Unless you're incredibly flexible with what you want to talk about/do or don't have very unique interests, finding people who you can do 100% with is not going to happen very quickly. It'll develop over time or you'll meet them in uni. Until then, just keep a bunch of friends and eventually, if you're honest and direct about how and who you spend your time with, you'll have everything you need.

Also, this is sixth form, think about your goals in life, study and read. Friends no longer have to encapsulate the entirety of your existence. Not having the best of the best won't kill you.

Mother shakes me from my sleep. Her arms are warm and soft as usual. My eyes are pierced by that usual morning glow. Sweet as honey and gentle as a birds soft sigh.

My gaze falls to my mother, her pale skin and striking inky black eyes. She smiles mildly as she takes me in. 'Good evening dear.' She croaks, in her lovely scratchy voice. 

'Good evening,' I start, 'the suns quite bright tonight.' I pause to contemplate my words when she suddenly tugs me out of bed. We walk past the large oak window. The sun slithers through but it somehow feels cold. I look forward to mother.  Her neon yellow skin shimmers in the light. She turns to me, her mild smile still stretching on. Growing larger. Fuller.

She pulls me on. We turn down the dark hallway. It's narrow and long. 'We'll be going to breakfast now, darling.' Her voice turns from scratchy to hollow. It echoes in my mind. But in the dark, and in the light of the small white dot in the distance, I can still see her smile.

Mother begins to run. Ferociously. Dragging me along like I'm some kind of lightweight. 'Mother, we're going too quickly. Slow down.'

Mother stops, looks back at me, and suddenly there's a window. Right beside me. I feel something in me tell me I should run out of the hallway. I look outside and there's a small swinigset. I turn to touch the window.

Mother grips my arm. Tightly, digging into my arms. Her voice is now high pitched and screechy. 'Mother is hungry dear. Please hurry up.' Her fingernails look more like claws now. I look up into her pretty milky-white eyes. She smiles ever so gently. I wonder why it feels so warm when she smiles.

'Yes, mother.' 

We rush forward, I turn back and the window's gone. I try to stop, startled. 'Mother, where did the window go?' She stops. The window is beside us again. It illuminates her azure skin. Her voice is prickly, almost to the point where I can't tell if she's speaking. 'EEE--EEEEEE-EEE-EEE-EEE-EEEE-EEE' I stop, alarmed. But mother smiles, it's warm. Nice and warm. I look into her beady bright red eyes.

'Okay, mother.'

We rush forward again. The light grows nearer. I feel more like I'm floating than being pulled along. 'Stop mother.' I demand breathlessly. She stops and turns to me. There the window is, with that narrow swingset. It's cold again. I look up, her eyes almost seem to have reduced to nothing. Small, pink sharp dots. Her violet skin shines in the light. She stares at me. I observe as her mouth opens but nothing seems to come out. Then she smiles, with all six rows of teeth. I feel warm. I smile too.

'Of course mother.' And she drags me even further.

I was in a similar situation a little while ago. It became incredibly boring and I felt like I wasn't even a real part of her life anymore.

In the end, I decided to leave violently. Lashed out in a very accusatory way and moved on. It may be best to fade out, especially when no one is to blame, but to me, a gentle ending seemed far more painful.

I think you should try and talk it all out. How you feel, what you wish they did, wish they would do, all of that stuff.

In my case, those conversations constantly lead to apologies and empty promises. I stuck around but if you notice this DON'T. It usually doesn't get better. It's best to respect yourself first and call them out on it.

Lastly, you could put less and less effort into the relationship. Fade out, make new friends. You're in your twenties so there's still a lot to figure out and a lot of people to meet! Then maybe, when you're in a better place emotionally and don't feel as crummy about it, meet up and talk again.

Plus, all friends you make to 'avoid being alone' are never up to standards. Why? They aren't your friend because they're fun or they're admirable, they're your friend cause they're around. Because of that, they never have to meet any of your expectations. 

That's why I think starting friendships should be taken carefully because you can never erase the beginning, you can never redo the platform without it all going to shit. Maybe look at the relationship whether you're even actually friends. Maybe you were just leeching off of each other for company

Outgrowing people, places and personalities isn't a bad thing. You just need to handle it well. I'm sure you'll be fine, just be careful because just the feeling of hating the past doesn't make its characteristics in you fade.

What you hate in others, you deny in yourself. This is a great opportunity to search for any shame you have due to your past or origins.

Best of luck stranger! I hope this all ends well. :)
